questions.question: What must you not do to a moving vehicle ahead of you inside crossing zig-zags?
options: Leave a two-second gap behind it
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 bans overtaking any leading moving or stopped vehicle at a crossing.

questions.question: Why do busy crossroads have yellow box junctions?
options: To stop queuing cars from blocking crossing traffic
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 keeps the centre of busy junctions clear for cross traffic.

questions.question: Why might a cyclist wobble or swerve slightly to the right?
options: To avoid potholes, drains, or gusts of wind
questions.explain: Rule 163: Cyclists need space to avoid drains and road hazards.

questions.question: At 30 mph on a dry road. How big should your gap to the car ahead be?
questions.explain: Rule 126: At least a two-second gap in dry weather.

questions.question: When should you avoid giving a signal?
options: When it could confuse or mislead other road users
questions.explain: Rule 103: Not to give misleading signals.

questions.question: Where do street lights usually show a 30 mph limit for cars. Unless signs say otherwise?
questions.explain: Rule 124: Street-lit roads default to 30 mph unless signed.

questions.question: What light appears immediately after red and amber?
questions.explain: Rule 175: The UK traffic-light cycle is red, then red and amber, then green.

questions.question: When turning right out of a side road onto a main road. Who must you give way to?
options: Traffic coming from both right and left
questions.explain: Rule 172: Checking and giving way to both directions when turning right.

questions.question: Who has priority at the top of the Highway Code hierarchy of road users?
questions.explain: Rule H1: Pedestrians are at greatest risk. Sit at the top of the road-user hierarchy.

questions.question: If you pass a side road you did not want, what should you do?
options: Drive on and find a safe place to turn
Reverse back up the main road
Stop in the middle of the lane
questions.explain: Rule 182: Never make a late swerve; carry on safely and turn later.

questions.question: Before moving back to the left lane after overtaking, what must you be sure of?
options: There is plenty of room ahead of the passed vehicle
The car behind flashes its lights
You are going at least 70 mph
questions.explain: Rule 133: Not to cut in front of the vehicle you overtook.

questions.question: After turning left or right into a side road, where should your car end up?
options: In the middle of the road
On the left side of that road
questions.explain: Rule 160: Always finish your turn on the left side of the new road.

questions.question: When approaching a roundabout, which side should you look to first for circulating traffic?
questions.explain: Rule 185: To give way to traffic coming from your right.

questions.question: How do you signal on approach when taking the first exit to the left?
questions.explain: Rule 186: A left signal on approach for the first exit.

questions.question: If you are taking the third exit. When do you switch to a left exit signal?
options: Just after passing the second exit
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 times the left signal right after passing the exit before yours.

questions.question: Where should the central island of a UK roundabout always stay?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 keeps the central island on your right as you travel clockwise.

questions.question: How is an ASL box marked on the road?
options: Two white stop lines with a cycle symbol between them
questions.explain: Rule 178: An ASL has a first stop line for motor vehicles. A second line ahead for cyclists.

questions.question: Why must you stop behind the white line rather than on the pedestrian crossing?
options: To keep the crossing clear and safe for people on foot
questions.explain: Rule 175: Stopping behind the line keeps pedestrians safe and out of traffic.

questions.question: What is wrong with forcing an oncoming driver to brake when you turn right?
options: It is safe if you signal
It is a serious fault and risks a head-on crash
questions.explain: Rule 180: Never cut across oncoming traffic and force it to brake.

questions.question: If another car is circulating alongside you in the next lane, what must you avoid?
questions.explain: Rule 186: Against drifting into another lane on roundabouts.

questions.question: What if a bus stops just before a zebra crossing to let someone cross? May you pass the bus?
options: No, you must wait behind the bus
Yes, pass slowly on the right
Yes, if you sound your horn
Only if no stripes are visible
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 bans passing the lead vehicle because it can hide pedestrians.

questions.question: You are turning right at a box junction. Your exit road is clear, but oncoming cars block your turn. May you wait in the box?
options: Yes, you may wait in the box to turn right
Only if you turn on hazard lights
questions.explain: Rule 174: makes a specific exception when turning right and waiting for oncoming traffic.

questions.question: If your indicator bulb fails before a drive, what should you do?
options: Fix it before driving, or use clear arm signals if safe
Use hazard lights for every turn
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 includes arm signals when indicators are not working.

questions.question: When you see temporary orange or red 50 mph roadworks signs. What is the legal limit?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 applies to temporary mandatory speed limits at roadworks.

questions.question: Who else needs similar wide clearance and slow passing speeds under Rule 163 / 215?
options: Horse riders and pedestrians walking in the road
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 gives wide, slow clearance to cyclists, horse riders, and walkers.

questions.question: When you stop in a queue behind another car, how much space should you leave?
options: Enough to see their rear tyres on the road
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 and queueing advice keep space to steer around if needed.

questions.question: If the lane you want to enter has faster traffic, what should you do?
options: Pull out and let them brake
Wait for a safe gap so they do not have to slow down
Signal for one second then steer
questions.explain: Rule 133: Waiting so faster vehicles do not have to slow down.

questions.question: What does keeping left help prevent on narrow residential streets?
questions.explain: Rule 160: Staying on your side leaves a clear path for oncoming drivers and cyclists.

questions.question: What should you do if a car is. Already on the roundabout to your right and close?
options: Stop behind the give-way line and wait for a safe gap
Accelerate hard in front of it
questions.explain: Rule 185: Waiting until there is a safe gap.

questions.question: When should you start your approach signal for a roundabout?
options: In good time before reaching the give-way line
After you are already on the roundabout
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 and Rule 103 require early, clear approach signals.

questions.question: Why should you not signal left before passing the exit before yours?
options: Drivers waiting at that earlier exit may think you are turning off and pull out
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 prevents early exit signals from misleading waiting drivers.

questions.question: If you want to make a U-turn at a roundabout, how must you do it?
options: Turn right immediately before the island
Drive all the way around the island clockwise and exit back
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 shows you must travel clockwise around the roundabout to return.

questions.question: Before moving off on green at an ASL, where should you check for cyclists?
options: Your nearside mirror and blind spot, and ahead
questions.explain: Rule 178: Check both ahead. To your left in case a cyclist is moving alongside you.

questions.question: What if you accidentally stop with your front bumper over the white line on red?
options: Stop and wait there without entering the crossing or junction
questions.explain: Rule 175: Never cross the junction on red; wait safely for green.

questions.question: When turning left from a side road onto a main road. Which direction is the main danger first?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 checks right first for nearside flow, and left for overtaking traffic.

questions.question: While waiting to turn right, where should your front wheels point?
options: Turned sharply right into the oncoming lane
Straight ahead until it is safe to turn
questions.explain: Rule 180: Keep wheels straight so a rear shunt does not push you right.

questions.question: What should you do if you realise you. Are in the wrong lane on a busy roundabout?
options: Follow your lane safely, take that exit, and turn around later
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 recommends staying safe in your lane rather than cutting across traffic.

questions.question: You are approaching a crossing and see a cyclist ahead inside the zig-zag lines. What should you do?
options: Hold back behind the cyclist until past the crossing
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 forbids overtaking any vehicle inside the zig-zag zone.

questions.question: You are turning right at a box junction. And the road you want to turn into is jammed full. May you enter the box?
options: No, because your exit road is blocked
questions.explain: Rule 174: only allows waiting in the box if your exit road itself is clear.

questions.question: What phrase helps drivers count two seconds cleanly?
options: Say 'Only a fool breaks the two-second rule'
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 suggests a steady two-second count past a fixed landmark.

questions.question: On a dual-lane exit roundabout where both lanes lead straight ahead. How should you pick your approach lane?
options: Use the left lane unless you are overtaking or signs direct otherwise
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 keeps traffic left unless overtaking or directed by markings.

questions.question: What if a cyclist ahead is in the left lane. Intends to turn right at the roundabout?
options: Give them room and do not overtake closely on the approach
Squeeze past them on the left
questions.explain: Rule 186: Cyclists may stay in the left lane even when turning right.

questions.question: Why do some large roundabouts paint route numbers like 'M6' inside the approach lanes?
options: To help you pick the right lane early for your destination
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 uses lane markings to guide drivers cleanly through big junctions.

questions.question: Approaching a blind hill crest behind a slow cyclist, what should you do?
options: Wait behind until you can see the oncoming road is clear
Overtake on the blind crest anyway
questions.explain: Rule 163: and Rule 166 forbid overtaking where you cannot see far enough ahead.

questions.question: Two side roads are close together on your left and you want the second one. When should you signal?
options: As you pass the first side road
100 metres before the first side road
After turning into the second road
questions.explain: Rule 103: Not to signal before an earlier turning you are not taking.

questions.question: If you drive down a steep hill. What must you watch to stay within the limit?
options: Your speed can creep up without pressing the accelerator
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 applies downhill too; use gears and brakes to stay legal.

questions.question: If a vehicle on the main road is flashing its headlights at you. What should you assume?
options: It is always safe to pull out
Wait until you are sure the way is clear and safe
questions.explain: Rule 172: means you stay responsible for pulling out only when it is genuinely safe.

questions.question: In slow queuing traffic, when should you change lanes?
options: Whenever a tiny gap opens for a moment
Only when it is safe and you will not block others
As fast as possible before the queue stops
Without signalling so others do not speed up
questions.explain: Rule 133: Not weaving between lanes or cutting across other drivers.

questions.question: What if the first exit is straight ahead and there is no left turn?
options: Treat it as straight ahead and do not signal on approach unless signs show left
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 matches your signal to the road layout and signs.

questions.question: After you have entered the exit road from a roundabout, what should you do?
options: Check your left signal has cancelled
Leave the left signal on for 300 metres
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 and Rule 103 require cancelling your signal once clear.
